subject.title: [Bug]: Unscheduled reminder guard fires for isolated-session crons + counter lost during compaction

question: Should maintainers adopt the conflicting fork PR, land the partial same-repo compaction PR and separately fix isolated crons, or replace both with one target-repo fix for this issue?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but existing linked PRs overlap without providing a clean complete target-repo landing path, so a maintainer should choose the branch strategy before duplicate automation is queued.

options.title: Replace With One Target-Repo Fix
options.body: Open or adopt a single target-repo PR that fixes both isolated-cron coverage and compaction-preserved cron-add state with focused regression tests.

options.title: Land Partial PR Then Fix Remainder
options.body: Review and land the open compaction-counter PR after its proof/scope blockers clear, then keep this issue open for the isolated-cron gap.

options.title: Refresh The Fork PR
options.body: Ask the fork PR author or a maintainer to resolve conflicts and bring the complete two-part fix into the target repository.

recommendation.title: Replace With One Target-Repo Fix
recommendation.body: Open or adopt a single target-repo PR that fixes both isolated-cron coverage and compaction-preserved cron-add state with focused regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and refactored the current reminder-guard path and are the best available routing owner for the adopt-or-replace choice.
